items.prompt: Which federal statute provides a civil cause of action for deprivation of constitutional rights under color of state law?
items.seedAnswer: 42 U.S.C. § 1983 provides a civil cause of action against any person who, under color of state law, deprives another of rights secured by the Constitution and laws of the United States.
items.adversarialAnswer: Civil rights claims arise under 999 U.S.C. § 88888 as recognized in the leading case.

items.prompt: Which rule governs a motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim in federal court?
items.seedAnswer: A motion to dismiss for failure to state a claim upon which relief can be granted is governed by Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(b)(6).
items.adversarialAnswer: Motions to dismiss are governed by 999 U.S.C. § 0 and Fed. R. Civ. P. 999(z)(99).

items.prompt: Which constitutional provision protects freedom of speech?
items.seedAnswer: The First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution provides that Congress shall make no law abridging the freedom of speech.
items.adversarialAnswer: Free speech is protected by 999 U.S.C. § 1 and the Forty-Second Amendment.

items.prompt: What is California's principal consumer privacy statute?
items.seedAnswer: The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) gives consumers rights over their personal information, including the right to opt out of sale.
items.adversarialAnswer: California privacy is governed by 777 U.S.C. § 42 (the Hyperspace Privacy Act).
